name: Pilates reformer
pattern: Pilates moves on a sliding carriage pulled back by springs: you push or pull the carriage away with control and resist the springs on the way back.
setup: Set the springs before you get on; ask an instructor for your first sessions.
Footwork: lie face up, head on the headrest, shoulders against the shoulder blocks.
Feet on the footbar hip width, knees bent, pelvis neutral.

steps.text: Breathe out and straighten your legs, pushing the carriage away in 2 counts.
Legs long but not locked; pelvis still on the carriage.
Breathe in and resist the springs as the carriage slides back in 3 counts; don't let it crash.

cues.cue: Control the return; the carriage never bangs the stopper.
cues.why: The return is eccentric work against the springs; letting go loses it and jolts the joints.

cues.cue: Pelvis and trunk stay still while the legs or arms move.
cues.why: Heavier springs gave more trunk and pelvis stability and more gluteus medius, oblique and multifidus work in side splits.

cues.cue: Heavier spring for stability, lighter spring for range and control.
cues.why: Lighter springs gave a larger, more even hip range but more trunk shift.

cues.cue: Knees track over the second toe; stop just short of locking.
cues.why: Same lower-limb alignment rules as squats and leg presses.

cues.cue: Out on the push, in on the return.
cues.why: Breath timing is the most used Pilates principle in research programmes.

breathing: Breathe out as you push the carriage away, in as it returns.

tempo.note: Push in about 2 s, return in about 3 s; 8-12 reps.

mistakes.name: Carriage crashes back
mistakes.looks: The carriage snaps home and hits the stopper.
mistakes.fix: Slow the return to 3 counts; lighten the spring if needed.
mistakes.why: Loses the eccentric work and jolts the joints.

mistakes.name: Pelvis rocks or tilts
mistakes.looks: The hips lift, tuck or shift side to side as the legs push.
mistakes.fix: Brace lightly, heavier spring, smaller range.
mistakes.why: The trunk is not holding; load moves to the low back.

mistakes.name: Knees snap straight
mistakes.looks: At full push the knees lock back hard.
mistakes.fix: Stop with the knees long but soft.
mistakes.why: Hyperextension loads the back of the knee.

safety: Get on and off only when the carriage is locked in at the stopper.
Standing work (side splits, standing lunges) needs light springs and an instructor until confident.
Osteoporosis: avoid loaded forward flexion like long spine and rolling moves.

variants.change: Feet on the bar on the balls of the feet: more calf work, ankles held high.
Heels on the bar: more glutes and hamstrings, feet flexed.
Legs straight, heels lower under the bar and rise: ankle only.

subtypes.name: Calf raises
subtypes.change: Legs straight on the footbar; lower the heels below the bar and rise onto the toes.

subtypes.name: Hundred
subtypes.change: Holding the straps, head and shoulders up, legs at 45°; straight arms pump by the sides against the straps.

subtypes.name: Frog, leg circles, long spine
subtypes.change: Feet in the straps: legs press out from a frog (heels together, knees wide) or draw circles; long spine rolls the hips over and down.

subtypes.name: Pelvic lift
subtypes.change: Feet on the bar, roll the hips up into a bridge, then press the carriage out and in from the bridge.

subtypes.name: Side split, Russian split and squat
subtypes.change: Standing with one foot on the platform and one on the carriage: push the carriage out into a wide straddle (side split) or a split stance, then pull it back with the inner thighs.

subtypes.name: Arm work (circles, chest expansion, overhead)
subtypes.change: Kneeling or lying, hands in the straps; pull the straps down past the hips (chest expansion), draw circles, or press overhead while the trunk stays still.

motion.basis: Default is footwork (lying leg press). Few kinematic studies exist; lee2023 (side splits, heavy vs light springs) informs trunk and spring cues. Angles are estimates from the standard repertoire. Members are few (14), so subtypes group them by body position.

sources.cite: Lee K. Motion analysis of core stabilization exercise in women: kinematics and electromyographic analysis. Sports (Basel). 2023;11(3):66.
Wells C, Kolt GS, Bialocerkowski A. Defining Pilates exercise: a systematic review. Complement Ther Med. 2012;20(4):253-262.
